message.content:
# Kimi K3 — Round 1

## A) Agenda answers

**Q1 (λ).** Keep fixed λ = 1. This is the one decision that is *not* post hoc: ablation9 was pushed before the run, fixed λ was its primary arm, and the preregistered comparison confirmed it (+27.05 vs +18.32). The econometric case is stronger than "within 2 SD": inner folds are smaller than the refit window, and optimal shrinkage grows with n, so nested CV systematically over-penalises the full-window refit — that is the −9.4 pp in 1970s–80s origins (λ = 30–100) and it is bias, not noise. Headline from 2027: the preregistered primary, fixed-λ walk-forward (expected ≈ +21 % per F35), with nested and oracle-free printed mandatorily beside it; no figure ever appears alone.

**Q2 (selection, gate).** Amend §4 formally: no per-origin selector is ever run; curve-only is operational by council lock. The selector's inner-CV advantage correlates with realised advantage at r = −0.16 and is carried by 6 rows from 1947–48 — it is a noise amplifier, and every non-degenerate variant loses 9–10 pp. Gate: two-tier, never switches anything. Δ = skill(F5) − skill(curve) on common walk-forward origins; |Δ| > 4.42 pp → council agenda; |Δ| > MDE_gate = 1.96 · SD_block(Δ), recomputed each refit by episode-block bootstrap (currently ≈ 21 pp) → stated as evidence. The gate's MDE must be printed next to the gate: a 21 pp bar with 8 onsets detects only catastrophe. Post hoc but acceptable: we follow a preregistered ablation whose prediction ("curve chosen from 2000") was *falsified* — that is the preregistration working, not us fitting results.

**Q3 (frequency).** Quarterly. The comparison is unpaired (different origin sets, different base rates); the paired evidence is the thinnings, of which phase 0 is *worse* than quarterly and the 0.02 pp failure is a knife-edge no decision should rest on. Decisive point: monthly origins overlap 11 months, quarterly 3 quarters — effective samples are ≈ 591/12 ≈ 49 vs 198/4 ≈ 50. Monthly adds no independent information; +2.19 pp < MDE 2.99 is consistent with that. Post hoc either way; status quo plus noise-level difference makes retention acceptable. Publish both readings of §2.

**Q4 (start).** Keep 1947Q2. On the 158 common origins the three starts differ by ≤ 1.4 pp — noise; the P spread (14.9/12.4/10.4) never changes the verdict. Moving now would be chosen knowing it cuts P 2.5–4.5 pp and costs up to 3 of 8 onsets — an irreversible power loss for a cosmetic gain. Acceptable despite being post hoc because we keep the locked constant, not a result-selected one. Print the three-start P line in every ledger row permanently.

**Q5 (demotion).** Documentation only. The incumbent set is an artifact of which symmetry one picks — "incumbent-as-challenger" yields curve-only, "+2/+2 on the drop effect" demotes nobody — so "5 incumbents pass" must be footnoted as rule-dependent wherever F5 is printed. Any future search (council mandate + sealed spec) uses one symmetric bar: a feature is dropped iff the drop gains ≥ +2/+2 pp, ≥ 7/8 LOEO folds at level, sign stable — the challenger bar applied to drops. E4's curve+cape (+29.69, fails G2/G3/G5, below MDE) stays dead.

**Q6 (content trigger).** Adopt from the 2027 refit. Exact rule: on each check, compute eligible_fit at current R; if it contains any positive label or relabel absent from the manifest, refit, pin, log. Cost: 18 net refits per 49 years; effect: 53/588 months changed, mean |ΔP| 0.13 pp, max 1.05 pp. Acceptable despite being post hoc because the effect is tiny and sign-neutral, and the rule removes a lag that depended on NBER's trough-announcement habits — an institutional accident, not economics.

**Q7 (ledger key).** Do not amend a single character; it was pushed before row 4, and the base-rate generosity (logged 22.8 % vs realised 15.3 %) and the censoring assumption are now known — changing either is goalpost-moving after the score. Publish a supplement with all four numbers side by side: engine censoring +24.41 %, no-USREC-vintage +28.95 %, oracle +33.28 %, ex-post pooled base rate +21.2 %, plus per-block skills and cluster-t 1.37 with block-bootstrap CI. Public statement, verbatim-worthy: "At 9 cycle blocks the ledger reaches 80 % power only after ≈ 150 years; naive tests reject a true null 36–53 % of the time at 5–20 years. The ledger is a transparency instrument; skill claims rest on the walk-forward."

**Q8 (EBP/Baa).** Close Baa-10y permanently unless redistribution rights are obtained — a public model with a local-file input is not reproducible, full stop. Defer EBP: the review has seen onset-aligned values at 6 of 8 onsets, so any spec written now is authored under contamination and its evidentiary value is permanently discounted; with MDE ≈ 4.4 pp and 3 pre-1990 onsets it is also near-powerless. Re-examine only after ≥ 12 monthly snapshots show a non-revising history, with the contamination disclosed in the sealed spec.

**Q9 (L_R).** Peak-only for the label floor: L_R = max over episodes of (peak announcement − peak) in months, floored at 18; trough announcements do not determine onset labels, and switching to all-announcements now would be chosen knowing it moves L_R to 21 and changes eligible origins — textbook post hoc. Separately, audit trough-announcement lags for the open-episode *censoring* rule, where they are the relevant quantity; that is a different parameter and must not be conflated with the floor.

**Q10 (ratification).** Ratify all four. Conditions: dual-logging of P on the published monthly figure (GS10 − TB3MS) continues until the 2027 refit settles the live-input definition; the minutes record that the live-input change and live censoring were made without mandate and are ratified ex post — the breach is noted, not blessed. The tripwire move restores an R3 decision and the log-day rule is already in the key; both trivially ratified.

## B) Verdicts on Claude's drafts

- **D1 — keep, amended.** Add the sample-size-scaling argument (inner-CV λ is biased upward for the full-window refit), and replace "fixed a priori" with "inherited constant, validated by preregistered ablation9". Headline = preregistered primary, mandatory triple print.
- **D2 — keep, amended.** Tier-2 MDE recomputed each refit from the block bootstrap of the paired Δ; the gate's own MDE printed beside every gate statement.
- **D3 — keep, strengthened.** The real reason is effective-sample parity and an unpaired headline comparison, not "status quo wins a tie".
- **D4 — keep, amended.** Three-start P line in every monthly ledger row, not just a sensitivity note.
- **D5 — keep, amended.** Specify *which* symmetry future searches use (challenger bar applied to drops); E4 shows the two symmetries give opposite answers, so "one symmetric bar" is ambiguous until pinned.
- **D6 — keep as written**, with the exact trigger definition from Q6.
- **D7 — keep, amended.** Add the ex-post pooled variant (+21.2 %) to the supplement and put the 150-year and 36–53 % figures in the public sentence itself, not a footnote.
- **D8 — amended.** Split: close Baa (redistribution is a hard constraint, not a deferral item); defer EBP with Claude's 12-snapshot condition plus mandatory contamination disclosure.
- **D9 — keep, amended.** Peak-only for the floor; commission a separate trough-lag audit for the censoring rule.
- **D10 — keep, amended.** Ratify all four with the dual-logging condition and the recorded-breach annotation.

## C) Biggest risk in my own proposal

My positions are uniformly status-quo-conservative, and that conservatism is itself a choice made after seeing that the status quo scores best. I am locking inherited arbitrariness — λ = 1 from v4's overlapping history, a 1947Q2 start with 24 quarters of spliced Shiller data and a 36.6 % base-rate era — while every monitoring instrument I endorse is too weak to catch decay: gate MDE ≈ 21 pp, ledger power at 150 years, bootstrap differences within 2 SD. If the 2022–24 failure mode (93.8 % false alarm) recurs after the 2027 refit, my framework will refuse to react and be unable to prove anything is wrong. That is a bet that 8 episodes generalise; I am taking it with open eyes.
message.reasoning:
Let me think carefully about this. I'm Kimi K3, a senior macro-econometrician on a council. I need to answer Q1–Q10, critique Claude's (Opus 5.5's) draft positions D1–D10, and state the biggest risk in my own proposal. Hard limit ~1200 words. Be concrete, quantitative, disagree openly.

Let me work through the evidence.

**E1 — λ selection.** Fixed λ=1 gives +27.05%; nested λ gives +18.32%. The nested selection loses −9.4 pp in 1970s–80s origins because inner CV picks λ=30–100 in early windows where the curve had negative inner skill pre-1966. Bootstrap difference −8.7 pp, SD 5.5 — within 2 SD, so not decisive statistically, but the sign and mechanism are clear: with 9–13 episode blocks, inner CV is noisy and over-penalises. Also the caveat: λ chosen on smaller inner folds over-penalises the full-window refit (λ optimal for n_inner is too large for n_full; standard result — optimal λ scales roughly with n). That's a real econometric argument: penalty choice is sample-size dependent, so nested CV on smaller folds systematically over-shrinks. Today CV picks λ=3, which barely changes P (15.1→15.8). So keep fixed λ. But Claude's concession that λ=1 isn't truly a priori is right; the honest framing: λ=1 is a protocol constant inherited, and the preregistered ablation9 tested nested vs fixed and fixed won. Since the ablation was preregistered before the run, choosing fixed λ now is *not* post hoc in the bad sense — it was the preregistered primary, and the preregistered comparison confirmed it. That's the key point: ablation9 was pushed before the run, so keeping λ=1 is following the preregistered plan, not cherry-picking. Headline number: I'd argue the headline should remain the preregistered primary metric: fixed-λ walk-forward +27.05% on 198 origins, with nested and oracle-free printed alongside. Actually, which should be the headline? The oracle-free +20.4% is the honest live-publishable number. But the headline skill of the model as a model is the walk-forward. I'd say: headline = fixed-λ +27.1% (preregistered primary), with mandatory companion figures nested +18.3 and oracle-free +20.4. Claude's D1 says print the pair plus oracle-free. Fine.

**Q2 — model selection and gate.** E1 shows per-origin nested selection picks F5 100% of origins from 2000 and delivers +8.52%, much worse. F5's inner-CV advantage is carried by one block (1947Q2–1948Q3, 6 rows, 4 positives — post-war inflation without inversion). Correlation between inner-CV advantage and realised advantage is −0.16 — the selector has no discriminative power; it's essentially noise, slightly perverse. So amend §4 formally: no per-origin selection; curve-only operational by council lock (already RAADETS_V501 §6). The gate: F5 benchmark printed; threshold question — borrowed 4.42 pp vs own MDE ~21 pp. The 4.42 is borrowed from the frequency test, clearly wrong for the gate; the gate's own MDE is 21.06 pp. A two-tier rule is sensible: >4.42 triggers agenda review (cheap tripwire), >21 constitutes evidence. But note gate difference currently −3.89 pp at 1947Q2 start (F5 worse), and the MDE 21–56 pp means the gate is nearly powerless — with 8 onsets you cannot detect economically meaningful differences. Honest statement: the gate can only detect catastrophic divergence. I agree with Claude's D2 mostly. Maybe sharpen: the tier-1 threshold should be recomputed as the gate's own MDE once the ledger/origins allow, or use a fixed pre-specified pp? Actually the two-tier as drafted is fine; I'd amend to state explicitly that tier-2 uses the gate's own MDE recomputed at each refit, and that the gate can never auto-switch — only council can.

**Q3 — frequency.** E2: full monthly +29.24% (591) vs quarterly +27.05% (198). Requirement: monthly ≥ quarterly − 1pp. Literal reading: passes (29.24 ≥ 26.05). Code reading (thinned m%3==0): 26.03 vs 26.05, fails by 0.02 pp — a knife-edge artifact of thinning phase; the other two phases pass. The full-minus-quarterly difference +2.19 pp with MDE 2.99 — not significant for v5.0.1 panel (legacy +3.01 exceeds its MDE 2.54). Also 591 monthly origins are overlapping 12-month windows — effective sample far smaller; the +2.19 pp is within noise. Both readings now known → post hoc either way. The blueprint §2's purpose was a gate to decide fit frequency before seeing results; now seen. Status quo (quarterly) is defensible; also the counterfactual monthly fit barely changes P (14.4 vs 14.9). But wait — should we actually switch to monthly because it passed the literal gate and has more origins? The danger: choosing monthly now because it scored higher is post hoc selection; the difference is within noise; the code reading fails. The honest decision: pre-commit to a rule. Since both readings are known, any choice is post hoc; the tie-break should be the principle "thresholds never relaxed after seeing results" — but here it's ambiguous which threshold. The literal blueprint text is the authority; the code was an implementation deviation. Hmm. The blueprint §2 text says "its own full monthly walk-forward" — the code deviated. Under the literal text, monthly passes. So one could argue: follow the blueprint's literal rule → monthly fit from 2027. But the gain is +2.19 pp within noise, and the choice is post hoc. Claude says keep quarterly, status quo wins ties. I could disagree here to show independence. Let me think about what's actually right econometrically.

Monthly fit: n_obs 800 vs 267, β −1.41 vs −1.29. More observations but heavily autocorrelated (overlapping 12-month label windows → effective n much smaller; with 12-month overlap, effective n ≈ 800/12 ≈ 67 independent-ish? Actually quarterly origins also overlap: 4-quarter horizon on quarterly origins gives overlap of 3 quarters; monthly overlap of 11 months. Effective sample for monthly ≈ 591/12×? — roughly comparable to quarterly's 198/4 ≈ 50 vs 591/12 ≈ 49. So information content is about the same!). That's a strong argument: the monthly fit adds almost no independent information; the apparent skill gain +2.19 pp is within the block MDE; and switching post hoc because it looks better is exactly the sin the council forbids. Keep quarterly. Also operational simplicity: ledger rows monthly but fit quarterly; the live input is already monthly. So I agree with D3 but for sharper reasons: effective sample parity, not just "status quo wins ties." Also the 0.02 pp failure of the code reading is a knife-edge; decisions should not hinge on 0.02 pp. And publish both readings.

Actually, let me reconsider: is there an argument that the blueprint's literal rule should govern, making monthly the preregistered-compliant choice? The blueprint §2 was written before; its literal text gates on the full monthly walk-forward. If we treat the blueprint as preregistered law, monthly passed and switching is following the preregistration, not post hoc. But the blueprint's gate was presumably evaluated in ablation3 with the thinned code — the actual preregistered test as implemented failed by 0.02 pp. The council already locked curve-only quarterly... The v5.0.1 model is quarterly. Hmm, "Curve-only is the operational model, locked by council decision (RAADETS_V501 §6)" — that's about features, not frequency. The frequency gate was a blueprint item. Given ambiguity, the cleanest defensible position: keep quarterly; rationale — (a) both readings known → post hoc; (b) difference within noise (2.19 < 2.99 MDE); (c) overlapping windows mean no real information gain; (d) knife-edge 0.02 pp is not a basis for change; (e) timeliness already handled by monthly live input. I'll agree with Claude but strengthen the reasoning. Or I could disagree and argue monthly. Being contrarian for its own sake is bad; the econometrics favors quarterly on effective-sample grounds. I'll keep quarterly.

**Q4 — universe start.** E3: start 1947Q2/1953Q2/1960Q1 → P today 14.9/12.4/10.4%; walk-forward on own origins +27.05/+30.28/+21.89; on 158 common origins +20.5/+21.4/+21.9. So on common origins the differences are small (+1.4 pp spread), within noise. Moving start now = chosen knowing it lowers P by 2.5–4.5 pp — post hoc. Also 1947Q2 uses Shiller LTR for 24 quarters pre-1953 — a data-quality argument for 1953Q2 exists a priori (GS10 starts 1953-04). But the change would be chosen after seeing effects. Pre-1960 origins are 36.6% positive vs 14.6% after — base-rate era mismatch. Hmm. The strongest argument to keep 1947Q2: it's locked, more episodes (8 onsets vs 5), and on common origins the skill is nearly identical; the P difference (14.9 vs 12.4) doesn't change the verdict (band contains base rate at every start). Also moving to 1960Q1 loses 3 of 8 onsets, devastating power. Keep 1947Q2, print sensitivity line. Agree with D4. Maybe add: preregister a rule that start changes only via council vote with sealed spec, and the sensitivity line (P at three starts) printed each ledger row? Printing three P's monthly is cheap and honest. I'd support that.

**Q5 — demotion.** E4: asymmetric rule kept 5 incumbents; symmetric "incumbent-as-challenger" demotes realrate, dd, d_infl (negative add-effects) and cape_pct fails folds; simultaneous/backward elimination → curve-only. Alternative symmetry (same +2/+2 on drop effect) → nobody demoted. So the set of incumbents is entirely an artifact of which symmetry you pick. Since curve-only is operational and feature search is closed, this matters only for documentation and for any future search. D5: document, and future search uses one symmetric bar fixed in sealed spec. Agree. Add: the F5 benchmark's continued printing should carry a footnote that its composition is rule-dependent; also the neutral-LL curve+cape result (+29.69, fails G2/G3/G5, below MDE) shows even the "best" alternative fails gates — no action.

**Q6 — content trigger.** E6: 18 net extra refits per 49 years; P differs in 53/588 months, mean |ΔP| 0.13 pp, max 1.05 pp. Removes 0–9-month lag in label incorporation. It's mechanical, deterministic, cheap. Adopt. But consider: more refits = more weight changes = more chances for arbitrary variation; but refits are deterministic given data. The lag asymmetry (delay depends on onset month) is a small bias. Adopt from 2027 refit. Agree with D6. One caveat: content trigger fires on relabels too (0 relabels historically due to 18-month floor). Fine. Also must define trigger precisely: eligible_fit at current R contains a positive label absent from manifest → refit. That's well-specified. Adopt.

**Q7 — ledger key.** E5: real-time censoring +24.41%, without USREC-vintage +28.95%, oracle +33.28%. The drop is 83 open-episode months including 1980-08..1981-05 run-up (P up to 96.6%). The logged base rate averages 22.8% vs realised 15.3% — the key's reference is generous to the model (easier to beat a high base rate? Actually log-loss improvement over pooled base rate: if the logged base rate is higher than realised, beating it is easier — generous). Preregistered reference +20.4%. Power: 80% power needs ~150 calendar years; naive tests reject true null 36–53% of time. So the ledger cannot deliver a verdict on any human horizon. Claude: don't amend the key (preregistered before row 4); publish E5 as supplement with all three censoring variants; state publicly the ledger is an honesty instrument, not a test. I agree strongly on not amending — amending a preregistered scoring key after seeing scores is the cardinal sin. But I'd add one amendment-consideration: the base-rate rule (a) "logged base rate in force" is generous (22.8% vs 15.3%). Should the key be amended to use ex-post pooled? No — preregistered; changing it now after seeing +24.41 vs +21.2 ex post would be moving the goalposts after the score is known. Publish both. Also the censoring: the engine's open-episode rule depends on a USREC-vintage assumption; publish all three. The public statement: "with 9 cycle blocks, cluster-t power reaches 80% only at ~150 years; therefore the ledger is a transparency device; skill claims rest on the walk-forward, not the ledger." Agree with D7, maybe strengthen: also publish per-block skills and the cluster-t with its CI annually. And state the minimum-3-blocks rule is necessary but not sufficient (reached with p=0.25 after 20y).

**Q8 — EBP/Baa.** E7/F37: contamination (review has seen EBP at onsets), EBP revisable residual, Baa non-redistributable, MDE 4.4 pp with only ~3 EBP onsets pre-1990 (8 total). Power hopeless: with 8 onsets and gate MDE 4.4 pp, and EBP's pre-1990 sample 3 onsets — a sealed test would almost certainly be uninformative; and the team has already seen the onset values, so any spec written now is contaminated. Claude: defer; re-examine after ≥12 monthly EBP snapshots show no revision. I'd go further: close EBP as a candidate for the curve-only era; the contamination is permanent (you can't unsee +0.59/+0.58 at 1990/2001 and −0.31/−0.51/−0.10 at 1980/2008/2020 — that's 6 of 8 onsets; anyone writing the spec knows where EBP helps). A sealed spec written by a contaminated author is not a clean test. Baa-10y: non-redistributable → violates reproducibility; close permanently unless licensing solved. So: close Baa until redistributable; defer EBP with Claude's 12-snapshot condition PLUS requirement that the sealed spec be written with a contamination statement, or better: the test, if ever run, must be labelled "spec written with knowledge of onset-aligned values" — which guts its evidentiary value. Honestly the right answer: close for 2027; revisit only if (a) 12+ snapshots show no revisions, (b) council accepts a contaminated-spec caveat. I'll say: close Baa, defer EBP with conditions — slightly stronger than Claude's defer-both. Actually Claude says defer both, re-examine after snapshots. Baa's problem isn't revision, it's redistribution — a permanent reproducibility violation for a public model. I'd strike Baa permanently (close), defer EBP. That's a concrete amendment to D8.

**Q9 — L_R.** Peak-only vs all announcements. The label is onset within 4 quarters; the 18-month floor exists to ensure the onset label is knowable in real time. What determines whether an onset label is knowable? The peak announcement. Trough announcements (1991: 20 months? lags 20–21 in 1991, 2001) don't change onset knowledge. But wait — does the trough announcement affect censoring of origins inside a recession? Yes: origins inside a recession are censored; in real time, "inside a recession" is known only after the peak announcement (which dates the peak, often before the trough is announced). The audit measures announcement lag L_R to set the floor. The floor's purpose: origins within L_R months before a known peak... Actually the floor ensures labels are mature: an origin's 4-quarter label is final only once any onset in the window would have been announced. Onset announcements = peak announcements. Trough announcements are irrelevant to onset labels. So peak-only is conceptually right. But: including trough announcements (lag 20–21) lifting L_R to 21 would be more conservative — it changes eligible origins. Is there a real-time information argument for trough announcements? The open-episode censoring rule: an episode stays open until the trough is announced? E5 mentions "day-precise announcement, final trough" as the USREC-vintage assumption. Hmm — the engine's open-episode rule censors months inside an ongoing episode; when does an episode close in real time? Arguably when the trough is announced (before that, you don't know the recession ended; USREC stays 1). So trough announcements matter for censoring, not for labels. The L_R audit is about the label floor though ("audit of the announcement lag... measured from the peak"). The question Q9: "Peak-only or all announcements?" For the label floor: peak-only. But for the censoring/open-episode rule, trough announcements are relevant. The cleanest: L_R for label maturity = peak-only (18 = floor, historical max peak lag? peak lags ≤ 12 < floor 18 per E6 — so floor 18 is already conservative). I'd answer: peak-only for the label floor; separately audit trough-announcement lags for the censoring rule, but that's a different parameter. Agree with D9 with that clarification. Also note: using all announcements would lift L_R to 21 and change eligible origins — a change chosen after seeing its effect (post hoc), another reason to keep peak-only.

**Q10 — F29 ratification.** Four changes: (1) live curve = trailing month of daily DGS10−DTB3 vs published monthly GS10−TB3MS — from row 3; every row from row 4 also carries P on the monthly figure. This is an operational change made without mandate. It's arguably an improvement (timeliness; daily Treasury par yields vs monthly averages; DTB3 vs TB3MS — both 3m T-bill, secondary market vs... DGS10/DTB3 are daily; the trailing-month average approximates the monthly average but available immediately). Since row 4 onward dual-logs, the ledger preserves comparability. Ratify, but require the dual-logging to continue indefinitely (or until 2027 refit). (2) swarm tripwires moved out of ignition column, restoring an R3 decision — a restoration of a prior ratified decision; ratify trivially. (3) log day = first weekday from 10th + 3 days — in the preregistered key already; ratify. (4) live censoring of readings inside announced recession — matches the engine's rule; ratify. So ratify all four, with the caveat that (1) must keep dual-logging P on the monthly figure until the 2027 refit decides the live-input definition, and a note that process violation (change without mandate) is ratified ex post but the process breach is recorded. Agree with D10 with that annotation.

Now — where do I disagree with Claude to show independence? Genuine candidate disagreements:

1. Q1 headline number: Claude wants the headline pair "fixed +x / nested +y" plus oracle-free. I could argue the headline should be the oracle-free +20.4% because it's the only number a live follower can actually verify... Hmm. Actually the published headline has been +27.05. The oracle-free supplement exists because some origins aren't live-publishable (oracle origins). For public honesty, the oracle-free figure is the one matching what the model could have said live. But the walk-forward on 198 origins is the preregistered primary. I think printing all three is right; the headline stays the preregistered primary. Not worth a fight; but I can sharpen: headline = preregistered primary (fixed-λ WF), and any public statement must carry all three; never headline the nested number alone (it undersells) nor fixed alone without companions.

2. Q3: I could disagree and pick monthly per the literal blueprint. But econometrics favors quarterly (effective sample parity). I'll keep quarterly but with sharper reasoning. Actually, let me reconsider once more — is there a real gain to monthly? β −1.41 vs −1.29; P 14.4 vs 14.9 today; skill +29.24 vs +27.05 on different origin sets (not paired!). "Full monthly and quarterly are scored on different origin sets with their own pooled base rates" — so +29.24 vs +27.05 is not even a paired comparison. The paired evidence is the thinned comparisons: phase 0 26.03 vs quarterly 27.05 (worse!), phases 1,2 better. So actually monthly thinning phase 0 is *worse* than quarterly. The full monthly +29.24 benefits from more origins (more frequent scoring of good periods?). This is weak evidence for monthly. Keep quarterly. Solid.

3. Q2: I'd amend D2 slightly: tier thresholds — tier 1 at 4.42 pp borrowed is arbitrary for the gate; but as a cheap tripwire it's fine. Keep.

4. Q7: agree, strengthen.

5. Q8: amend — close Baa permanently (redistribution is a hard reproducibility constraint), defer EBP with the 12-snapshot condition plus mandatory contamination disclosure; note the deeper problem: even a sealed spec now is written by contaminated authors; the test's evidentiary weight is permanently discounted. Also power: MDE 4.4 pp with 8 onsets; EBP pre-1990 3 onsets → G5-style subperiod gates would be near-powerless. Defer is right; close is cleaner for Baa.

6. Q9: agree peak-only, add the trough-audit-for-censoring distinction.

7. Q4: agree, add mandatory permanent three-start P line in each ledger row (cheap honesty). Claude says "print the start-sensitivity line permanently" — same thing. Fine.

8. Q6: agree; add precise trigger definition and a cap: content-triggered refits also occur on relabels; require the refit to be byte-deterministic and logged; 18 refits/49y is acceptable. Also note the trigger removes a subtle look-ahead asymmetry: delay depended on trough-announcement timing, i.e., on NBER's communication, not on the economy — good riddance.

Biggest risk in my proposal: Keeping λ=1 fixed and quarterly/1947Q2 status quo, justified by "post hoc" conservatism, entrenches inherited arbitrary choices (λ from v4 overlapping history; 1947Q2 with 24 quarters of Shiller LTR spliced data; 36.6% base rate era) and refuses ~+2 pp monthly skill and a steeper β; if the next cycle resembles 2022–24 (curve inversion without onset, or the 1970s where nested λ lost 9.4 pp), the frozen configuration's skill may degrade and every safeguard we have (gate MDE 21 pp, ledger power 150 years) is too weak to detect it in time. I.e., the biggest risk: the council's conservatism is itself a post-hoc choice (we've seen status quo looks best), and the model's monitoring instruments are too underpowered to catch decay — we're locking a configuration whose only strong evidence is backtest skill concentrated in a handful of episodes. Also the 2022–24 false alarm (93.8%) shows the curve-only model's known failure mode; nothing in my answers addresses it. That's honest.

Alternatively, the single biggest risk: by keeping fixed λ=1 on the strength of a preregistered ablation whose margin (−8.7 pp, SD 5.5) is under 2 SD, and by refusing monthly fit, we may be locking in a suboptimal-but-lucky configuration; and the ledger can't adjudicate for 150 years. I'll formulate crisply.

Word budget: ~1200 words. Q1–Q10 at 2–6 sentences each ≈ 10 × ~60 words = 600; B) verdicts ≈ 350; C) ≈ 120. Tight. Let me draft efficiently.

Let me make sure I include formulas/procedures where I specify computations:
- Q1: headline = preregistered primary; procedure: at each refit print triple (fixed-λ WF skill, nested-λ WF skill, oracle-free), same 198-origin protocol extended.
- Q2: gate two-tier: Δ = skill(F5) − skill(curve) on the common walk-forward origins; tier1 |Δ| > 4.42 → agenda; tier2 |Δ| > MDE_gate = 1.96·SD_block(Δ) (episode-block bootstrap, 9 blocks) → evidence. Currently MDE ≈ 21.06.
- Q3: effective sample argument: quarterly 198 origins with 4q overlap → ~198/4 ≈ 50 independent; monthly 591 with 12m overlap → ~49; no information gain; keep quarterly.
